entryContext.question: Whose hand writes the ledger's corrections?

message.text: I put the 1820 and 1901 pages side by side under the archivist's lamp. Same hesitation before the descenders, same refusal to close the g. And one more thing: on Charter Night, one bell failed, and nobody has said which.

The hand is settled canon now — CANON-050 records that it belongs to neither writer. The bell is not settled. Charter Night's sequence is a charter clause, and a clause that fails silently is either maintenance or message. I have raised it as a thread rather than guessed.

candidates.title: Which bell failed on Charter Night — and why did nobody hear it fail?
candidates.rationale: The sequence is a charter clause and this year it broke for the first time in living memory. The record should hold the question before the town explains it away.

draft.title: Which bell failed on Charter Night?
draft.question: The sequence has rung complete for two hundred years. This year one bell did not sound, the silence was seven minutes long either way, and no fault has been found in the mechanism. Which bell — and is the failure in the bell, or in what listens for it?
